nodes.name: Iron foam cleaning and a/c-FeOOH formation
nodes.procedure: Foam iron of 2×3 cm² is washed in acetone, 3 M HCl, and ethanol for 10 min, respectively. Next, the clean iron foam is soaked in ethanol for 10 min and then ignited in a laboratory environment to obtain a/c-FeOOH/IF.
nodes.source_text: Foam iron of 2*3 cm² is washed in acetone, 3 M HCl, and ethanol for 10 min, respectively. Next, the clean iron foam is soaked in ethanol for 10 min and then ignited...

nodes.name: Ru doping of a/c-FeOOH/IF
nodes.procedure: a/c-FeOOH/IF is immersed in 5 ml absolute ethanol solution with 5 mg RuCl3 for 10 min and then ignited again in a laboratory environment to obtain a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF.
nodes.source_text: a/c-FeOOH/IF is immersed in 5 ml absolute ethanol solution with 5 mg RuCl3 for 10 min and then ignited again...

nodes.name: Phosphorization of a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF
nodes.procedure: 1 g NaH2PO2 and a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF are placed in the upstream and center of the quartz tube, respectively. Heated at 400°C for 2 h at a heating rate of 2°C min⁻¹ in an N₂ atmosphere to obtain the final a/c-Ru-FeP/IF.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-FeP/IF shows massive structure with thicker nanosheets; a/c-Ru-FeP/IF shows coral structure uniformly covered with nanorod array resembling coral velvet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a shows that the a/c-FeP/IF catalyst is a massive structure with thicker nanosheets growing. Fig. 2b further proves that a large number of nanosheets grow on the surface of a/c-FeP/IF catalyst ... Surprisingly, the as-prepared a/c-Ru-FeP/IF (Fig. 2d-e) is a coral structure uniformly covered with a nanorod array.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-FeP/IF shows obvious amorphous and crystal regions in nanosheets; a/c-Ru-FeP/IF shows distinct crystalline and non-crystalline regions with fine particle size causing aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further magnification of the nanosheets in a/c-FeP/IF (Fig. 2c and S10) shows that there are obvious amorphous regions and crystal regions in a/c-FeP nanosheets ... Fig. 2f shows the a/c-Ru-FeP coral structures that have been ultrasonically exfoliated from the IF substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-FeP/IF shows lattice fringes of 0.2540 nm, 0.1919 nm, and 0.2047 nm attributed to (200), (210), and (201) planes of Fe2P; a/c-Ru-FeP/IF shows lattice fringes of 0.2048 nm, 0.1920 nm, and 0.1730 nm for (201), (210), and (002) planes of Fe2P with lattice expansion due to Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal region has lattice fringes of 0.2540 nm, 0.1919 nm, and 0.2047 nm, which are attributed to the (200), (210), and (201) crystal faces of Fe2P ... There are 0.2048 nm, 0.1920 nm, and 0.1730 nm lattice fringes in the crystal region, which are attributed to the (201), (210), and (002) crystal faces of Fe2P, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru element is uniformly dispersed on a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst; Fe, P, and Ru elements are uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the same time, the Mapping (Fig. 2h) also proves that Ru element is uniformly dispersed on a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst ... Fig. 2h and Figure S14 confirm that Fe, P, and Ru elements are uniformly dispersed on the a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-Ru-FeP/IF exhibits superhydrophilicity with contact angle of 0°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As expected, the contact angle of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF with the H2O droplets is only 0° (Fig. 2i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Both a/c-FeP/IF and a/c-Ru-FeP/IF composed of Fe2P (PDF#65-1990) phases and amorphous materials; peaks in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF show negative shift due to Ru doping into Fe2P lattice; both show wide amorphous peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a proves that both a/c-FeP/IF and a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalysts are composed of Fe2P (PDF#65-1990) phases and amorphous materials. The difference is that compared with a/c-FeP/IF, the peaks belonging to Fe2P in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalysts all show a negative shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-Ru-FeP/IF shows Ru 3d peaks at 280.0 eV and 284.3 eV (Ru 3d5/2), Ru 3p at 461.98 eV and 485.38 eV (Ruδ+), Fe 2p Fe-P at 707.55/721.00 eV and Fe-O at 711.05/721.3 eV, P 2p P-M at 129.3/130.75 eV and P-O at 133.55 eV; Fe-P peaks negatively shifted vs a/c-FeP/IF confirming Ru→Fe electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3b, the two main peaks located at 280.0 eV and 284.3 eV are associated with Ru 3d5/2 ... Fig. 3c shows that the peaks of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF at 461.98 eV and 485.38 eV are attributed to Ruδ+ species ... As demonstrated in Fig. 3d, there are three groups of peaks in the Fe 2p spectrum of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF. The peaks at 707.55 eV and 721.00 eV are attributed to Fe-P ... In the P 2p spectrum of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF (Fig. 3e), the peaks at 129.3 eV and 130.75 eV attribute to P-M, and the peak at 133.55 eV corresponding to P-O ... Importantly, the peaks corresponding to Fe-P components in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF are negatively shifted compared to a/c-FeP/IF.

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-FeP/IF shows H3O+ peaks at ~1750 cm⁻¹ increasing and H2O peaks at 1600 cm⁻¹ weakening at -0.16 V; a/c-Ru-FeP/IF shows more obvious H3O+ peaks and Ru-H peak at 878 cm⁻¹ appearing and increasing with voltage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4a-c show the Raman spectrum of a/c-FeP/IF with applied voltage ... Compared with Fig. 4d-f, it can be found that the peaks attributed to H3O+ intermediates in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF are more obvious ... Fig. 4g-i more directly proves that the H proton is transferred to the Ru@a/c-interface sites for hydrogen desorption ... characteristic peak at 878 cm⁻¹ attributed to the Ru-H bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-O-H peak at 531.3 eV increases and adsorbed H2O peak at 533.0 eV decreases with applied voltage reaching maximum Fe-O-H at -0.16 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures S18 and S19 show that when the applied voltage of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst is 0 V, the characteristic peak belonging to Fe-O-H species at 531.3 eV is the smallest, while the characteristic peak belonging to adsorbed H2O (at 533.0 eV) is the largest.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru mass fraction in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF is 0.0016%; after 100 h stability test, Fe content in electrolyte is 0.0993 mg/L for a/c-Ru-FeP/IF vs 0.1204 mg/L for a/c-FeP/IF after 20 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Table S4, the mass fraction of Ru in a/c-Ru-FeP/IF ... is 0.0016% ... By detecting the contents of Fe and Ru in electrolyte solution after the stability test (Fig. 5g and Table S9), it is found that the content of Fe in the electrolyte of a/c-FeP/IF catalyst is as high as 0.1204 mg/L after the stability test for 20 h. Surprisingly, after the 100 h stability test of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst, the content of Fe in the electrolyte solution is only 0.0993 mg/L.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF is 38.44 mF cm⁻², higher than a/c-FeP/IF (35.08 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 5d, the Cdl value of the a/c-Ru-FeP/IF catalyst in HER is 38.44 mF cm⁻². It is much higher than that of a/c-FeP/IF (35.08 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rct of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF is 0.217 Ω, lower than a/c-FeP/IF (2.019 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 5e and Table S6 show that the Rct value of a/c-Ru-FeP/IF is 0.217 Ω for HER, which is lower than that of a/c-FeP/IF (2.019 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: a/c-FeOOH/IF precursor shows wide amorphous peak and FeOOH (PDF#01-0662) diffraction peak; a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF shows amorphous FeOOH and crystalline FeOOH with negative shift of FeOOH peaks due to Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding XRD pattern (Figure S7) shows that the as-synthesized a/c-FeOOH/IF precursor has a wide peak belonging to the amorphous material and a diffraction peak belonging to the FeOOH (PDF#01-0662) phase ... Figure S9 demonstrates that the a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF catalyst is still composed of amorphous FeOOH and crystalline FeOOH. However, compared with the a/c-FeOOH/IF catalyst, the diffraction peaks of the FeOOH phase in the a/c-Ru-FeOOH/IF catalyst have a certain negative shift.
